accepted.s:
With reference to the India Semiconductor Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2021.
2. It provides for a Production Linked Incentive of ₹76,000 crore.
3. ₹65,000 crore has been committed under the mission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in 2021, provides a ₹76,000 crore PLI, and has ₹65,000 crore committed under it.
accepted.tq: Use the statement-code method to verify each figure and date independently.
accepted.sec: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the status of projects under the India Semiconductor Mission mentioned for the period under consideration?
o: 24 DLI projects, six chip units under construction and an OSAT pilot line at Morigaon
21 DLI projects, four chip units under construction and an OSAT pilot line at Bengaluru
23 OSAT projects, five fabs under construction and a DLI pilot line at Dholera
23 DLI projects, five chip units under construction and an OSAT pilot line at Sanand
accepted.x: The mission has 23 Design Linked Incentive projects, five chip units under construction, and an OSAT pilot line at Sanand in Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Separate the project count, construction count and location instead of treating them as one figure.
accepted.sec: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Semicon 2.0, regarded as the second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, was notified with an outlay of:
accepted.x: Semicon 2.0 was notified with an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Semicon 2.0 outlay from the earlier mission’s ₹76,000 crore PLI.
accepted.sec: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six pillars of Semicon 2.0?
accepted.x: The six pillars are Design; Machines and materials; Fabs; Packaging; R&D; and Talent. Drone services is not a semiconductor pillar.
accepted.tq: Find the option belonging to a neighbouring technology theme rather than the listed framework.
accepted.sec: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the incentives under Semicon 2.0:
1. CMOS silicon fabs may receive up to 40% capital subsidy.
2. Compound and display fabs may receive up to 35% capital subsidy.
3. Advanced OSAT/ATMP units may receive up to 35% support.
4. Conventional packaging may receive up to 25% support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The stated support levels are 40% for CMOS silicon fabs, 35% for compound/display fabs, 35% for advanced OSAT/ATMP and 25% for conventional packaging.
accepted.tq: Match each percentage to its exact facility category before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Semicon 2.0, the maximum support indicated for R&D and the additional engineering talent target are respectively:
accepted.x: The R&D pillar provides support of up to 75%, while the Talent pillar aims to add one lakh more engineers.
accepted.tq: Pair the percentage with the associated human-resource target.
accepted.sec: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As of January 2026, which one of the following combinations is correct for the results associated with semiconductor development?
o: 24 design startups, 112 academic tape-outs, 65 chips at 180 nm and 297 universities under Chips to Startup
24 design startups, 122 academic tape-outs, 56 chips at 180 nm and 397 universities under Chips to Startup
20 design startups, 122 academic tape-outs, 56 chips at 180 nm and 397 universities under Chips to Startup
23 design startups, 122 academic tape-outs, 56 chips at 90 nm and 397 universities under Chips to Startup
accepted.x: The reported figures are 24 design startups, 122 academic tape-outs, 56 chips fabricated at 180 nm, and 397 universities reached by Chips to Startup.
accepted.tq: Check every numerical component; a single altered figure makes a combination incorrect.
accepted.sec: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Processor)
 a. DHRUV64
 b. SHAKTI
 c. AJIT
 d. Vikram 3201

List-II (Developer)
 i. IIT Bombay
 ii. ISRO’s Semi-Conductor Laboratory, Chandigarh
 iii. C-DAC
 iv. IIT Madras

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: DHRUV64 was developed by C-DAC, SHAKTI by IIT Madras, AJIT by IIT Bombay and Vikram 3201 by ISRO’s Semi-Conductor Laboratory, Chandigarh.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure developer–processor pair and eliminate codes containing a repeated mismatch.
accepted.sec: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about indigenous processors is correct?
o: AJIT is a 32-bit space-grade processor developed by ISRO’s Semi-Conductor Laboratory.
Vikram 3201 is a 64-bit processor developed by IIT Madras for automotive use.
DHRUV64 is a 64-bit RISC-V processor intended for 5G, IoT and automotive applications.
SHAKTI is a conventional non-RISC-V processor developed by C-DAC.
accepted.x: DHRUV64 is a 64-bit RISC-V processor developed by C-DAC for 5G, IoT and automotive applications. Vikram 3201 is the 32-bit space-grade processor associated with ISRO’s laboratory.
accepted.tq: Watch for swapped developers, bit sizes and application areas.
accepted.sec: Semiconductor Mission - fabs/OSAT → state, indigenous chips → developer  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Drone Rules, 2021, a drone weighing more than 150 kg is classified as a:
accepted.x: The 2021 weight classification defines a drone above 150 kg as a large drone.
accepted.tq: Use the weight-range boundary rather than the drone’s purpose to identify the class.
accepted.sec: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding drone weight classes under the Drone Rules, 2021:
1. Nano drones weigh up to 250 g.
2. Micro drones weigh more than 250 g and up to 2 kg.
3. Small drones weigh more than 2 kg and up to 25 kg.
4. Medium drones weigh more than 25 kg and up to 150 kg.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the nano, micro, small and medium weight classes under the 2021 Rules.
accepted.tq: Read the upper and lower boundaries carefully, especially at 250 g, 2 kg, 25 kg and 150 kg.
accepted.sec: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations represents the principal types of UAVs identified in the classification?
accepted.x: The types identified are fixed-wing, multi-rotor and hybrid VTOL. Nano, micro, small, medium and large are weight classes, not types based on design.
accepted.tq: Separate design-based UAV types from weight-based classifications.
accepted.sec: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Drone swarms are best described as:
o: Large drones operated manually by a single pilot from different locations
Many drones coordinated by software for surveillance, light shows or strikes
Drones restricted exclusively to agricultural spraying
Fixed-wing aircraft that cannot exchange operational data
accepted.x: A drone swarm consists of many drones coordinated through software and may be used for surveillance, light shows or strikes.
accepted.tq: Choose the definition that captures both coordinated operation and the stated applications.
accepted.sec: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a measure identified for making India a global drone hub by 2030?
o: A ban on DGCA-approved training institutes
Production Linked Incentive for drones and components
accepted.x: The measures include liberalised Drone Rules, 2021, DigitalSky, PLI, Drone Shakti, DGCA-approved training institutes and Bharat Drone Mahotsav. A ban on such institutes is contrary to the stated approach.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that reverses a supportive policy into a restrictive one.
accepted.sec: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: The DigitalSky platform associated with drones is primarily an:
accepted.x: DigitalSky is the online permission platform included among India’s drone-sector measures.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a regulatory digital platform from manufacturing, subsidy and defence applications.
accepted.sec: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Kisan drones are primarily associated with which of the following activities?
o: Operating light shows and conducting strikes
accepted.x: Kisan drones are used to spray crops and map land; 100 were flagged off in February 2022.
accepted.tq: Link the named agricultural technology to its direct field applications.
accepted.sec: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Namo Drone Didi initiative is associated with providing drones to:
o: women’s Self-Help Groups for agricultural services
DGCA training institutes for flight certification
accepted.x: Namo Drone Didi provides drones to women’s Self-Help Groups for agricultural services.
accepted.tq: Identify the beneficiary group and purpose together rather than relying on the programme name alone.
accepted.sec: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which district was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing under the stated Andhra Pradesh proposal?
accepted.x: Sri Sathya Sai district, near Bengaluru, was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing.
accepted.tq: Use the precise district-location association; do not substitute a nearby technology centre.
accepted.sec: Drones and UAVs - types, swarms, rules, PLI, Kisan drones, Namo Drone Didi, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Additive manufacturing differs from subtractive machining because it:
o: builds an object layer by layer from a digital CAD model
changes the shape of materials only after exposure to sunlight
removes material from a solid block until the final shape is obtained
uses only biological materials for fabrication
accepted.x: Additive manufacturing builds objects layer by layer from a digital CAD model, whereas subtractive machining removes material.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the opposed processes by asking whether material is added or removed.
accepted.sec: 3D printing - additive manufacturing, applications  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with an application of 3D printing?
o: Health — replacement of all conventional medicines
accepted.x: The listed applications include custom-shaped food, health-related prosthetics and implants, construction, automotive prototypes and aerospace parts.
accepted.tq: Prefer the option stating a specific practical use rather than an extreme replacement or prohibition.
accepted.sec: 3D printing - additive manufacturing, applications  [other exams]

accepted.s: India’s first 3D-printed post office, mentioned in connection with additive manufacturing, was located in:
accepted.x: India’s first 3D-printed post office was located in Bengaluru in 2023.
accepted.tq: Pair the landmark with its city and year without confusing it with an industrial application elsewhere.
accepted.sec: 3D printing - additive manufacturing, applications  [other exams]

accepted.s: What is the distinguishing feature of 4D printing?
o: It uses four separate printers to produce one object.
It adds materials that change shape over time.
It prints only four-dimensional maps for navigation.
It removes four layers from a machined object.
accepted.x: 4D printing adds materials designed to change shape over time.
accepted.tq: Break the term into its functional idea: printed material with time-dependent change.
accepted.sec: 3D printing - additive manufacturing, applications  [other exams]

accepted.s: Additive manufacturing is identified as a course area under:
accepted.x: Additive manufacturing is one of the course areas under FutureSkills PRIME.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a skilling programme from semiconductor and drone-sector initiatives.
accepted.sec: 3D printing - additive manufacturing, applications  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Term)
 a. PLC
 b. SCADA
 c. Digital twin
 d. Cobot

List-II (Meaning)
 i. Virtual replica of a physical object or system
 ii. Collaborative robot working safely beside humans
 iii. Rugged industrial computer controlling machines
 iv. Remote monitoring of plants and grids

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: PLC controls machines as a rugged industrial computer; SCADA enables remote monitoring; a digital twin is a virtual replica; and a cobot works collaboratively with humans.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive acronym meanings and then verify the remaining pairs.
accepted.sec: Automation terms - PLC, SCADA, digital twin, cyber-physical systems, cobots

accepted.s: A virtual replica of a physical object or system used for simulation and monitoring is called a:
accepted.x: A digital twin is a virtual replica of a physical object or system used for simulation and monitoring.
accepted.tq: Match the application—simulation and monitoring—to the exact automation term.
accepted.sec: Automation terms - PLC, SCADA, digital twin, cyber-physical systems, cobots

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a cyber-physical system?
o: A rugged computer used only to control one machine
A robot designed exclusively for light shows
A virtual replica used only for simulation
Computing tightly integrated with physical processes
accepted.x: A cyber-physical system integrates computing closely with physical processes and is a core element of Industry 4.0 and the NM-ICPS mission.
accepted.tq: Distinguish system-level integration from the narrower meanings of PLC, digital twin and robot.
accepted.sec: Automation terms - PLC, SCADA, digital twin, cyber-physical systems, cobots

accepted.s: A factory robot designed to work safely beside human workers is known as a:
accepted.x: A cobot, or collaborative robot, is designed to work safely alongside humans.
accepted.tq: Infer the term from the workplace scenario and the word ‘collaborative’.
accepted.sec: Automation terms - PLC, SCADA, digital twin, cyber-physical systems, cobots

accepted.s: The World Economic Forum’s proposed Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre in Andhra Pradesh would be India’s:
o: first such centre after Mumbai and Telangana
fourth such centre after Bengaluru, Mumbai and Telangana
third such centre after Mumbai and Telangana
accepted.x: The proposed centre in Andhra Pradesh would be India’s third, after the centres in Mumbai and Telangana.
accepted.tq: Count the ordinal position from the explicitly named earlier locations.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Industry 4.0 context is correct?
1. Andhra Pradesh has an Industry Policy 4.0.
2. IIITDM Kurnool ranked first in the Department of Telecommunications assessment of 100 5G Use Case Labs for January–June 2026.
3. Efftronics and JNTU Kakinada launched an industry-sponsored M.Tech in IoT.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh has an Industry Policy 4.0, IIITDM Kurnool topped the stated 5G Use Case Labs assessment, and Efftronics with JNTU Kakinada launched an industry-sponsored M.Tech in IoT.
accepted.tq: Check each AP-specific institutional fact separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following best expresses the principal criticism associated with automation and artificial intelligence?
o: They replace only manual work and have no effect on intellectual work.
They eliminate the need for all forms of industrial training.
They replace intellectual as well as manual work, raising the issue of job displacement.
They are confined to semiconductor fabrication and do not affect employment.
accepted.x: The criticism is that automation and AI can replace both intellectual and manual work, thereby raising concerns about job displacement.
accepted.tq: Select the option that captures both dimensions of the employment concern without an absolute overstatement.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
